name: Bill of supply
definition: A bill of supply is the document issued under clause (c) of section 31(3) in place of a tax invoice. Rule 49 fixes eight particulars, (a) to (h). It carries no rate of tax and no amount of tax, because there is no tax to state.
why_it_exists: It is how a supply that carries no output tax is documented. The absence of tax fields is the point, not a defect — an extraction system that demands a tax rate on every supplier document will reject every lawful bill of supply.
inputs: whether the supply carries output tax
outputs: the set of rule 49 particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
preconditions: the document is a bill of supply referred to in clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 31
exceptions: a document issued under another Act in respect of a non-taxable supply is treated as a bill of supply
an electronic bill of supply under the Information Technology Act, 2000 needs no signature
rule 46A permits a single invoice-cum-bill of supply for mixed taxable and exempt supplies to an unregistered person
common_mistakes: demanding a rate of tax or an amount of tax — rule 49 lists neither
rejecting a foreign or other-Act document for a non-taxable supply — the second proviso to rule 49 deems it a bill of supply
assuming a bill of supply carries no HSN — clause (e) requires it
legal_references: UNKNOWN — clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 31 of the CGST Act, which fixes WHEN a bill of supply is issued, is a different document and was not read for this record
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: whether the supply is taxable or exempt or non-taxable
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not name itself, because a bill of supply and a tax invoice differ in what they must contain
weak when it is unknown whether the supplier is a composition taxpayer or the supply is exempt
validation_checks: all eight particulars (a) to (h) are present, unless the signature is excused as an electronic bill of supply
the serial number is at most sixteen characters
no rate of tax or amount of tax is demanded
examples: a composition taxpayer's document showing supplier GSTIN, serial number, date, recipient details, HSN, description, value and signature, with no tax shown — rule 49 satisfied
counterexamples: a document with no Harmonised System of Nomenclature Code — clause (e) fails

evidence.quote: 49. Bill of supply.-A bill of supply referred to in clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 31 shall be issued by the supplier containing the following details, namely,-
value of supply of goods or services or both taking into account discount or abatement, if any; and

Provided further that any tax invoice or any other similar document issued under any other Act for the time being in force in respect of any non-taxable supply shall be treated as a bill of supply for the purposes of the Act.
